title: Beyond Mobility: Modelling Residents’ Preferences for Livable, Equitable and Climate-Responsive Urban Neighbourhoods
content: Urban neighbourhood policies are commonly evaluated through separate transportation, environmental, housing and digital-service indicators even though residents experience these characteristics jointly and face trade-offs between them. This paper develops an integrated framework for evaluating preferences for safe, inclusive and climate-responsive neighbourhood renewal, with particular relevance to hot-arid urban environments. It combines a multi-attribute neighbourhood discrete choice experiment with a respondent-level attitudinal measurement system. The empirical demonstration uses 720 adult respondent records, eight stated-choice tasks per respondent, and three alternatives per task, yielding 5,760 choices and 17,280 alternative records. A conditional logit model, a panel latent-class model, cost-based compensating variations, and a two-stage composite-based structural path model were estimated from the generated data. Protected street safety, affordability safeguards, green and shaded streets, local public spaces and better transit access all increased the probability of choosing an improved neighbourhood, whereas monthly costs reduced support. A two-segment specification revealed a larger safety–shade–accessibility-oriented group (63.8%) and an affordability-oriented group (36.2%). The structural analysis explained 38.2% of the variance in the neighbourhood-livability acceptance score. The empirical estimates are based on survey responses from adult participants and provide evidence of their preferences regarding livable, equitable and climate-responsive neighbourhood development in Muscat. This integrated framework demonstrates how choice-based and attitudinal evidence can be linked while keeping behavioural preferences distinct from stated intentions. The study provides a complete survey design, equations, model comparisons and analytical reporting architecture for a future field investigation.
